title: Private deploy: time synchronization and package authenticity contract
creator: Avery Chen
description: Define deterministic requirements and acceptance criteria for Private/VPC deployments focused on two related failure domains: (1) host and operator time synchronization in zero-or-limited-egress environments, and (2) offline package authenticity verification during staged upgrades. Goal is to eliminate class of upgrade failures caused by clock skew and unsigned or corrupted artifact installation while preserving air-gapped constraints.
background: Field incidents and canary runs show intermittent upgrade failures in isolated VPCs originating from clock drift on operator nodes or mismatched timestamps used to validate signed artifacts. Customers with strict egress policies prefer staged delta images and signed bundles; however signature verification currently assumes reasonably synchronized clocks and online CRL/OCSP checks. This PRD consolidates requirements for deterministic time behavior and offline authenticity verification so upgrades succeed under zero-egress or controlled-egress modes.
goals: 1) Provide clear operational contract for acceptable clock drift, time sync strategies (NTP/PTP/local-GPS), and upgrade gating when clocks are out-of-tolerance. 2) Define an offline signature verification protocol for package bundles that works without OCSP/CRL by supporting embedded signatures, signed manifest checksums, and optional KMS/HSM verification. 3) Produce acceptance tests and rollout checklist for Private deployments and operators to validate on customer sites.
non_goals: 1) Implementing a full PKI issuance workflow for customers. 2) Building a custom time source hardware. 3) Requiring customers to expose broad egress for live OCSP/CRL checks except in documented fallback modes.
constraints: - Must work in air-gapped and minimal-egress configurations. - Avoid adding calls to external internet-based revocation services by default. - Any cryptographic verification must be compatible with customer KMS/HSM or local public key bundles. - Changes should be compatible with current operator and bootstrap flows and not require kernel-level modifications.
requirements: R1: Time sync contract: operator must detect host clock skew > 120s and refuse to start control-plane upgrade actions until drift is corrected or operator is placed into manual-maintenance mode.
R2: Supported sync strategies must include: NTP clients with fallback to preseeded drift tolerances, optional PTP support, and documented procedures for manual time set in fully air-gapped sites.
R3: Upgrade bundles must include a signed manifest file containing: artifact checksums (SHA256), build timestamp (ISO8601), signing key id, and optional embedded certificate chain.

R4: Signature verification must support two modes: online verification (OCSP/CRL) when egress permitted, and offline verification using either: (a) pre-uploaded revocation list snapshot, (b) embedded signed timestamp from a trusted signing authority, or (c) local public key pinned by customer via bootstrap.

R5: Operator must expose diagnostics and explicit failure reasons when signature or checksum validation fails; diagnostics must include expected signature key id, computed checksum, and artifact manifest timestamp.

R6: Operator must support a deterministic upgrade gating FSM: PRE-VALIDATE -> QUORUM-PRECHECK -> STAGE -> CANARY -> ROLL. Time and signature checks are part of PRE-VALIDATE and must be atomic preconditions for progressing.

R7: For customers using customer-managed KMS/HSM, operator must accept a signature-verification hook that executes verification inside the customer's HSM and returns boolean pass/fail and a short auditable message.

R8: Provide a maintenance-window choreography that tolerates up to 15 minutes of transient unavailability for health probes while upgrades are applied, with rollback triggers defined by error rates and probe timeouts.

R9: Documentation must include step-by-step air-gapped operator bootstrap sequence: how to seed trusted public keys, how to stage revocation snapshots, and how to perform manual time correction with audit traceability.

R10: Logging and audit: time-sync events, drift corrections, signature verification decisions, and operator modes must be written to local audit log and optionally exported to customer SIEM. Logs MUST include RFC3339 timestamps and signature key fingerprints.

R11: Backwards compatibility: Existing private deployments without preseeded keys must continue to be supported via a documented manual approval flow (operator unlock with human confirmation and recorded justification).
R12: Test harness: provide an automated test scenario that simulates clock drift, revoked-signed-artifact, and missing-CRL cases and validates operator behavior in each.
R13: UX: Console must show per-site time-health, last-known-verification-key, and last-upgrade-manifest-hash for audit and support workflows.
R14: Security: All signature verification code paths must be memory-safe and avoid loading untrusted code during verification; any third-party verification binaries must be sandboxed.
R15: Performance: Manifest verification for a typical bundle (<2GB) should complete within 30s on customer operator hardware baseline (4 vCPU, 8GB RAM).
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Unit and integration tests cover pre-validate FSM states, including failure modes for clock-drift, invalid-signature, and missing-manifest, with test coverage >= 85% for verification logic.

AC2: End-to-end upgrade test in an air-gapped lab with pre-seeded public keys and no external egress succeeds for full control-plane upgrade and records audit trail for time-sync and signature checks.

AC3: If host drift >120s, operator remains in PRE-VALIDATE and surfaces a clear remediation path in logs and console. Automatic progression only allowed after manual confirmation or after drift corrected and verified.

AC4: Offline verification mode must be exercised by a customer lab test that uses a revocation snapshot that includes one revoked key; operator must reject artifacts signed by revoked keys and accept artifacts signed by valid keys.
AC5: Verified performance: manifest verification completes within 30s on the baseline hardware in 95th percentile of test runs.
AC6: Console surfaces site-level indicators: time-health (OK/WARN/FAIL), last-verified-manifest-hash, and verification-mode (online/offline/manual) for all private sites during an upgrade.
AC7: Documentation: onboarding doc and runbook published in central docs repo and linked from console; runbook includes step-by-step manual override procedure and operator diagnostic commands.
AC8: Security review: internal security team approves the offline verification design and HSM/KMS integration with any open findings addressed or triaged.
AC9: Customer acceptance: at least two pilot customer sites (one fully air-gapped, one controlled-egress) complete a staged upgrade using the new contract and sign-off the runbook.

AC10: Telemetry: operator emits metrics for time-drift-detected, verification-failures, verification-mode, and manifest-verify-latency; metrics are present in the console and exportable to customer telemetry endpoints.
AC11: Rollback behavior: if signature verification fails during STAGE or CANARY, operator aborts rollout and returns to PRE-VALIDATE with clear diagnostics and no partial image application.
AC12: Manual approval flow: documented manual unlock flow works and produces an audit record with operator, approver, timestamp, and reason.
AC13: Test harness automation: provided test scenarios run in CI for both online and offline verification mode and pass deterministically in >= 9/10 CI runs under simulated network variance.
AC14: Backcompat: existing private deployments without preseeded keys can complete an upgrade using the manual unlock flow and record audit traces per the runbook.
AC15: No high-severity security regressions are introduced as verified by SAST and dependency SBOM review.

AC16: Documentation for customer troubleshooting includes explicit guidance for sensors commonly observed in the field: NTP service failure, PTP misconfiguration, and operator container exceeding host time drift threshold.
AC17: Operator exposes a dry-run verification mode that validates manifests and signatures without mutating state; dry-run must produce same pass/fail diagnostics as actual run.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: implement verification primitives and time-drift detector, ship to canary private operator images. Phase 2: partner with two pilot customers (air-gapped and controlled egress) to validate offline revocation snapshot workflow. Phase 3: GA release with docs, runbook, and console UX flags. Include opt-in 'strict-time-check' feature flag for customers who want automatic enforcement.
monitoring_and_metrics: Emit metrics: private.site.time_health (OK/WARN/FAIL), private.site.manifest_verify_latency_seconds, private.site.verification_failures_total{reason}, private.site.drift_detected_total. Logs must include structured fields: site_id, node_id, event, timestamp, verification_key_fingerprint.
rollback_criteria: Automatic rollback to previous control-plane version if: a) CANARY shows >3x baseline error rate for 5 minutes, or b) any verification-failure occurs in >1% of nodes in STAGE. Manual rollback requires two approvers and audit record.
operational_runbook: Include runbook sections: 1) Diagnose time-health and steps to correct NTP/PTP, 2) How to seed public keys and revocation snapshots, 3) How to perform offline verification using provided tools, 4) Manual unlock workflow and audit commands, 5) Emergency rollback and data-collection scripts for support.
supporting_notes: - Prefer manifest-embedded signatures (detached+bundle) to relying on live OCSP. - We will produce a small reference utility for customers to generate revocation snapshots from their PKI for offline verification. - Interview with 3 pilot sites scheduled week of 2026-03-15 to validate maintenance window expectations.
next_steps: 1) Engineering spike for time-drift detector and HSM signature hook (2w). 2) Draft runbook and console UX mocks (1w). 3) Security review kickoff and threat model (1w). 4) Schedule pilot validations with two customers (asap).
